neighbours.label: a comma that closes a clause and hands off to another clause (e.g. after 'Although it was a little heavy at first,' or 'touted his bona fides,')
fire: DeSantis went on to tout his bona fides, noting that under his administration, Florida has signed the strongest law.
Although it was a little heavy at first, the backpack felt fine after an hour on the trail.
When the rain finally stopped, the children ran outside to splash in the puddles.
The senator touted his bona fides, insisting that nobody had fought harder for farmers.
Because the bakery opened late, we grabbed coffee at the station instead.
She studied the map for a long time, then folded it and started walking north.
If you leave the oven on, the cake will burn before dinner.
The engine sputtered twice, and the old truck rolled to a stop.
quiet: The backpack felt a little heavy at first but fine after an hour on the trail.
The children ran outside to splash in the puddles when the rain finally stopped.
The senator touted his long record of fighting for farmers.
We grabbed coffee at the station because the bakery opened late.
She studied the map for a long time before walking north.
The cake will burn before dinner if you leave the oven on.
The old truck sputtered twice and rolled to a stop.

predictions: Expect a fail or a marginal result: the pole is weak and diffuse; only the concessive and bona-fides commas probed above exceeded 0.3.
